cities: One store, in Portland · independent shops, and its own site

craft_evidence.owned: Probable, claim-level: knits its own worsted wool "on 1940's knitting machines" (Full-Throttle Moto-Sweater page); trim "knit at Dehen factory" (All-City Leather Jacket, N-1 Deck Jacket pages); factory page narrates a Dehen-built mill and apparel factory at Flanders & 10th, NW Portland (1960-80) but does not state the current site; Heddels (press, 17 Dec 2020) quotes president Jim Artaiz: knits its own 100% wool fabric on 1950s flatbed machines. No filing, photo-of-site or tour read.
craft_evidence.makers: Columbia Knit (Portland) named as knitter/cutter/sewer on Heavy Duty Baseball Tee and Portland Rugby Shirt pages; elsewhere "Made in Portland" without a maker named.
craft_evidence.mills: Abraham Moon & Sons, UK (Skyline Overshirt Donegal Silt); Halley Stevensons, Scotland (Woven Chore Coat dry wax cotton); Gitman collab oxford "milled in Portugal" (mill unnamed). Wool yarn and cotton suppliers not named.
craft_evidence.madein: 15 of 15 men's product pages read state Portland, Oregon/USA (tees, knitwear, outerwear, overshirts, collab oxford); 15 of an estimated ~45 styles
craft_evidence.heritage: Dated and placed: Dehen Knitting Company formed 1920 in Portland, Oregon by William Peter Dehen (ex-Jantzen); varsity jacket 1951; Dehen 1920 line launched 2011 (brand history pages).
craft_evidence.process: Partly: "knit by us on 1940's knitting machines", "Extra heavy four-end jersey knit", varsity jackets "by hand"; Heddels (press): seven employees and about six hours per sweater. No stage-by-stage page.
craft_evidence.reasoning: Real, dated, placed heritage and own knitting on vintage machines for the knitwear that is the brand's core, with named UK mills on woven pieces. Held at 4 not 5: tees and rugby shirts are made at Columbia Knit (a named third party), woven jackets are cut-and-sewn with no stated ownership of that floor, and the current factory site and ownership of the building are not shown. Confidence medium.

ownership.owner: Brand says family-owned, "well into our fourth generation" (History page, no owner named). Heddels (press, 17 Dec 2020) names Jim Artaiz as president and owner. Not reconciled.

opview: “We are a family business known for long-lasting quality, workmanship and rugged styling.” — Dehen Knitting Co. (the house, writing as itself), Dehen 1920, History page
